prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of the Mugwump of Lake Timiskaming, a lake monster with a horse's head and a serpent's body.
ANATOMY: ONE unmistakable HORSE HEAD with long equine muzzle, two HORSE EARS, TWO natural dark eyes, short wet horse mane at top of neck; head directly joins ONE long LIMBLESS SCALED SERPENT BODY with single tapering tail, no horse torso, no legs, fins, flippers, horns or wings. Total length OVER TWENTY FEET, not hundred-foot giant [mugwump-folklore-c04,mugwump-folklore-c09].
MOMENT: Rear the thick front of the serpent body through the lake surface and lean horse head toward viewer with nostrils flared and mouth open in a horse bellow; remaining long legless body undulates behind in one clear broad S bend, water slides from wet muzzle and scales.
POWER: no documented visible power; movement physically displaces lake water, no magic breath or aura.
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme water-level close angle; equine head and thick scaled serpent front fill square, distant EMPTY canoe on shore contextualizes 6m-plus length, no victims.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one warm sunset shaft through cloudy lake sky rims horse ears, wet mane and dark scales, deep walnut water shadows, ordinary spray.
SURFACE: wet dark equine muzzle and mane merging into rough black-bronze serpent scales, textured cold freshwater.
SETTING: Lake Timiskaming on Ontario-Quebec border, dark Canadian forest shoreline secondary [mugwump-folklore-c01].
MOOD: dangerous imposing hybrid lake monster in active surfacing, never ordinary swimming horse, cute seahorse mascot, calm animal or distant landscape.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from any film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline or energy ribbons. Premium painterly brushwork, dark warm walnut and antique gold palette, square composition.
name: Mugwump (folklore)
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native and 200px inspected: one horse head with two equine ears/eyes/long muzzle and mane joins clearly scaled thick legless serpent body and single trailing S-curve/tail. No horse legs/torso or fish fins mixed; horse teeth natural rather than predator fangs. Active rearing bellow/spray and hybrid body unmistakable at 200px, boat secondary scale context. No text/aura/victims. Seven Sangar checks pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and head/teeth, coils and distant-canoe crops. One unmistakable horse head (mugwump-folklore-c09) with two upright horse ears, two dark eyes, flared nostrils and a wet dark mane; the white forehead star is editorial. The mouth is open in a bellow, showing horse incisors and pointed canine tushes. The head joins directly to a thick, limbless, scaled serpent body (c09), with no horse torso, legs, fins or wings. It rears out of the lake toward a water-level camera, throwing spray, while the rest of the body loops in coils through the surface behind, giving a length well over 20 feet (c04). The setting is a wide northern lake with a dark conifer shoreline at sunset (Lake Timiskaming, c01), with a small canoe beached far off on the shore and no one attacked. No text or aura. The horse head on a serpent body, the bared teeth and the rearing lunge make it a dangerous hybrid lake monster at 200px, not an ordinary swimming horse or a cute seahorse.
